#  METADATA Data Description:  
#
#  Filename: USGS.Circular1291.Appendix6.GW.data.txt
#
#  The water-quality data provided herein are the principal ground-water data summarized in USGS 
#  Circular 1291, The Quality of Our Nation's Waters:  Pesticides in the Nation's Streams and Ground
#  Water, 1992-2001
#  URL http://ca.water.usgs.gov/pnsp/pubs/circ1291/
#
#  Analytical data for 75 pesticides and 8 degradates at 5,047 ground-water monitoring sites are provided
#  in this tab-delimited data file. Ground-water sites in 51 Study Units were selected in accordance 
#  with the NAWQA national design strategy. Sites were classified into four land-use groups (agriculture,
#  urban, undeveloped, or mixed) on the basis of the design of each ground-water study. That is, all sites
#  in agricultural, urban, or undeveloped land-use surveys were classified as agricultural, urban, or undeveloped
#  land use, respectively, and all sites in major-aquifer surveys were classified as mixed land use.
#  Ground-water samples were collected from 187 land-use and major-aquifer studies. Data anaylses were
#  based on one sample per well. One sample from well 401658074505001 was used in both the delrsus1 and linjsus3 studies.
#
#  A detailed discussion of methods and approaches used for pesticides in ground water for Circular 1291,
#  including site selection, land-use classification, sample-collection, laboratory analysis, and data
#  processing and analysis is presented in Appendix 8.
#  URL http://ca.water.usgs.gov/pnsp/pubs/circ1291/appendix8/
#
#  Pesticide names, CAS numbers, and other characteristics are presented in Appendix 1A.
#  URL http://ca.water.usgs.gov/pnsp/pubs/circ1291/appendix1/
#
#  A list of ground-water monitoring sites are presented in Appendix 5.
#  URL http://ca.water.usgs.gov/pnsp/pubs/circ1291/appendix5/
#
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
#  METADATA Update:
#
#  Prior to January 29, 2008 concentration values for pesticides not detected in a sample were inadvertantly listed
#  as the maximum common reporting level (MAXCRL) for water years 1992-2002 (see appendix 8). These values were updated 
#  to the maximum long-term method detection level (MAXLTMDL) for water years 1992-2002 (see appendix 8) on January 29, 2008.
#

#	Attribute label: Rnnnnn (All variables of the form Rnnnnn, where nnnnn is the 5-digit parameter
#                         code used to identify variables in the USGS National Water Information System)	
#	
#	Attribute description: Remark code associated with each parameter value
#       Source: NAWQA Data Warehouse water-quality data retrieval 3-29-2002
#	
#                Code     Description	
#                -----    --------------------------------------------------------------------------------	
#                <        Not Detected. Value reported as less than the Long-Term Method Detection Level.	
#                (blank)  Detected.	
#                E        Detected. Concentration is estimated. Estimated concentration may result from	
#                         any of the following reasons:	
#                         1. The compound is characterized as a ""poor performer"" in the method on the 	
#                            basis of laboratory QC samples. In general compounds with less than 60 %	
#                            recovery, greater than 120 % recovery, or greater than 25 % relative standard	
#                            deviation of recovery are considered poor performers. All detections of	
#                            these compounds are remarked E.	
#                         2. The compound was detected at a concentration less than the reporting level	
#                            or less than the lowest calibration standard.	
#                         3. The sample was diluted to bring the concentration into the calibration range.
